key_insight: A fixed-weight linear-attention transformer can exactly replay one update step of a standard acyclicity-constrained causal discovery algorithm, so stacked blocks reproduce its optimization trajectory.
engineering_relevance: This shows transformers can serve as deterministic algorithm executors for causal-structure learning, but accurate execution is distinct from recovering the true causal graph.
method: Construct a transformer block that carries the current graph state and the optimization multiplier across updates.
Prove the block exactly matches one iteration of the reference continuous causal discovery method.
Analyze stage-wise update counts and numerical error behavior to bound rounding drift as depth increases.
evidence_signal: The constructed block matches the reference update to floating-point precision; replay on synthetic data and seven benchmark network topologies mirrors the solver’s successes and failures.
watch_item: Exact execution depends on preserving the multiplier state, and standard attention models under the tested training budgets did not reliably generalize to larger graphs.
paper_title: Executing Causal Structure Learning with Linear-Attention Transformers
